attribution.note: Zitron's own arithmetic in his own post. He quotes The Information only for the subscriber inputs.

semantics.note: This is arithmetic on stated premises: an assumed $5 Go price and the reported subscriber counts. Both qualifiers are kept, the unit is not inflated, and the acquisition superlative is treated as an aside.

contract.note: Reading the unit as monthly is the ordinary reading, since both prices are monthly. Requiring the inputs to be verified is reasonable. Excluding ads and the $8 price matches his own setup.

evidence.note: OpenAI's January 2026 launch page confirms the $20/month Plus price. It does not establish the 44M/9M or 3M/112M subscriber counts, so it cannot verify the scenario inputs.

reviews.rationale: The arithmetic is correct: 35M x $20 minus 109M x $5 = $155M per month. But the contract requires independent verification of the reported subscriber inputs. The original report was inaccessible, and the only admissible item confirms just the Plus price. His own quotation of The Information cannot verify itself, so the inputs remain unverified.

attribution.note: This is Zitron's own characterisation of what OpenAI's reported projections mean.

semantics.note: An observation about the content of OpenAI's reported forecasts. Dropping the rhetorical 'somehow' does not change the commitment.

contract.note: Reading 'primary business line' as the largest revenue product line is an ordinary reading. Allowing Plus-to-Go migrations to count toward the 109M is fair to his words.

evidence.note: A secondary summary from April 29 reports the projected 80% Plus fall to about 9M and a roughly 36-fold Go rise to 112M. That implies about 109M added. It does not establish that Plus is the primary revenue line, and it is not the original report.

reviews.rationale: A secondary summary weakly corroborates the projection part: Plus falling about 80% and Go rising to 112M. The support condition also requires showing that Plus was OpenAI's largest revenue line, and the packet has no product revenue breakdown. The original report could not be read, and nothing contradicts the claim. Because one required element is unverified, the claim cannot be fully assessed.

attribution.note: Zitron describes the thesis of his own piece and endorses it as one of his best.

semantics.note: 'Will kill' is unhedged, so this is a scorable forecast. No deadline was given.

contract.note: Reading 'kill' as corporate failure principally caused by OpenAI dealings is an ordinary reading of the metaphor. It is not stretched, though the speaker supplied no threshold. Leaving the forecast unresolved until a decisive event is fair given there is no deadline.

evidence.note: Oracle's October 27, 2026 press release shows continuing operations and an expanded OpenAI partnership. It neither shows failure nor permanently closes off the claimed causal pathway.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. No Oracle corporate failure occurred by the cutoff, and nothing permanently closes off the OpenAI-driven pathway. Oracle still operating is not failure of an open-ended forecast, so the claim cannot yet be scored.
